questions.stem: If A > B, B = C, C ≥ D, then which is definitely true?

options.option_text: A > D, by chain of inequalities
A < D, the reverse direction here
A = D, equality from chain steps

questions.explanation: Combine: A > B, B = C, so A > C. C ≥ D, so A > C ≥ D → A > D (definitely true). Distractor 2 is opposite. Distractor 3 only equality if D = C and B = A, but A > B, not =, so equality is impossible. Distractor 4 — B = C ≥ D, so B ≥ D (could be B = D, never B < D).
questions.subject: Quant

questions.stem: If P ≥ Q, Q > R, R = S, S ≤ T, which is NOT necessarily true?

options.option_text: P > R, definitely from given chain
P > T, NOT definitely from chain

questions.explanation: P ≥ Q > R = S ≤ T. So P ≥ Q > R = S, hence P > R, P > S, Q > S — all definite. But for P vs T: we have P ≥ S (since P > S follows). And S ≤ T means T could be larger or equal to S. So T could be > P (if T is much larger) or T ≤ P. Hence P > T is NOT guaranteed. ✓

questions.stem: If x is an integer and 2x + 5 < 17, the LARGEST possible value of x is:
questions.explanation: 2x + 5 < 17 → 2x < 12 → x < 6. Largest INTEGER < 6 is 5. Verify: 2(5)+5 = 15 < 17 ✓. 2(6)+5 = 17 NOT < 17. Distractor 6 = boundary exclusion error. Distractor 7 = wrong direction. Distractor 4 = answered ≤ 5 wrongly.

questions.explanation: 3y − 7 ≥ 2y + 5 → 3y − 2y ≥ 5 + 7 → y ≥ 12. Verify y = 12: 3(12)−7 = 29; 2(12)+5 = 29. 29 ≥ 29 ✓. y = 13: 32 ≥ 31 ✓. Distractor 2 — used 7 + 2 wrongly. Distractor 3 — wrong sign direction. Distractor 4 — wrong both.

options.option_text: x ≤ −4, sign FLIPS on negative divide

questions.explanation: −2x ≥ 8 → divide both sides by −2. CRUCIAL RULE: when multiplying/dividing both sides of an inequality by a NEGATIVE number, FLIP the inequality sign. So x ≤ 8/(−2) = −4. Verify x = −5: −2(−5) = 10 ≥ 8 ✓. x = −4: −2(−4) = 8 ≥ 8 ✓. x = 0: 0 ≥ 8 ✗.

questions.stem: If 5 < x < 12 and x is an integer, the SUM of all possible values of x is:
questions.explanation: Strict inequalities: 5 < x < 12 → x ∈ {6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11}. Sum = 6+7+8+9+10+11 = 6×(6+11)/2 = 6×17/2 = 51. Distractor 68 = if you wrongly include 5 + 12: that gives 5+6+...+12 = 8×17/2 = 68. Distractor 63 = arithmetic slip. Distractor 75 = miscount.

questions.stem: If a < b < c and all are positive, then which is largest in 1/a, 1/b, 1/c?
questions.explanation: For positive numbers, smallest denominator → largest fraction. a < b < c (a smallest), so 1/a > 1/b > 1/c. Reciprocal REVERSES order for positive numbers. Example: a=2, b=3, c=4 → 1/a = 0.5, 1/b = 0.33, 1/c = 0.25. So 1/a largest.
